**Surah al-Nasr (The Divine Support)**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿When the help of God comes, and the victory﴾. As for *al-nasr*, it is *al-ma'una* (aid), derived from their saying, "The rain has supported (*nasara*) the land," when it helps its vegetation and keeps it from drought. The poet said:

*When the sacred month has passed, bid farewell to the lands of Tamim, and set out for the land of Amir.*

Regarding what is meant by this support, there are two opinions:

The first: it is the support of the Messenger against the Quraysh. This was said by al-Tabari.

The second: it is his support over every enemy who fought him, for the final outcome of the support was his.

It was also said: "When His support comes" means His making you prevail over your enemies. *Al-fath* (the victory) is the conquest of Makkah. It was also said that what is meant is when God supported the believers and opened Makkah and the rest of the lands to them.

The attainment of the matter was expressed by "coming" as a figurative usage, to indicate that the decreed matters are directed at their specified times, so that they become known little by little. The support has drawn near in its strength, so be watchful for its arrival and prepared to give thanks for it.

Regarding this victory there are two opinions:

The first: it is the conquest of Makkah. This was said by al-Hasan and Mujahid.

The second: it is the conquest of cities and palaces. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas and Ibn Jubayr. It was also said that it is what God opened to him of knowledge.

The first: they are the people of Yemen. It is related from Ibn 'Abbas that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Religion is from Yemen, jurisprudence is from Yemen, and wisdom is Yemeni." The second: its meaning is that God relieved His Prophet of distress through the people of Yemen, who are the Ansar.

The second opinion: they are all the nations that entered Islam. This was said by Muhammad ibn Ka'b.

Al-Hasan said: When God granted His Messenger Makkah, the Arabs said to one another, "O people, you have neither a favor with Him nor with the people." So they began entering the religion of God in throngs, nation after nation.

The first: He accepts repentance.

The second: He overlooks minor sins.

The first: that this be from him a thanks to God, the Exalted, for His blessings, because the renewal of blessings requires the renewal of thanks.

The second: that it was an announcement to him of his own death, so that he would exert himself in his work.

Then there was revealed ﴿And fear a Day when you will be returned to God﴾, and he lived after it twenty-one days.

Muqatil said: He lived after it seven days. And God knows best. The blessings of God be upon him continuously, without cessation, through the passing of ages and the turning of times, and upon all the prophets and messengers.
